newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Tesco offers cut-rate Mexican Levis.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tesco offers cut-rate Mexican Levis.

text.p: Britain's biggest supermarket group Tesco Plc has triggered an investigation at jeans giant Levi Strauss & Co after launching sales of the company's jeans at cut prices, company sources said on Thursday.
Tesco said it had bought 45,000 pairs of the men's jeans direct from a Levi factory in Mexico.
"It has raised several issues that we are investigating," said a spokeswoman from Levi's, whose trademark denim jeans are sought-after commodities around the world.

Tesco started selling the jeans at 150 of its 500 or so stores on March 24 at 30 pounds ($48.85) a pair compared with prices of between 45 and 55 pounds or higher often charged by designated Levi retailers.
"They have been selling extremely well and in some stores we have already sold out," a Tesco spokeswoman said. "We are trying to sort out emergency deliveries."
The company said it had been trying to deal directly with Levi's for several months but had been told it was deemed an "inappropriate" outlet.
Asked how Levi Strauss had reacted, Tesco said: "Well, you'll have to ask them but I don't think they're very chuffed."
Levi Strauss is the leader in Britain's 1.2 billion a year pound denim market and thus very keen on protecting and promoting its brand.
It held talks with Tesco a year ago on the possibility of the supermarket stocking its jeans, but Tesco failed to meet the company's quality and objectives criteria, the Levi spokeswoman said.
But she added that Tesco had been told it could approach Levi's again if circumstances changed.
Newspaper reports on the row suggested Levi Strauss objected to its jeans being sold next to groceries.
Levi Strauss said it advised customers to buy from authorised stockists where staff were specially trained and a full range of jeans was available.
The spokeswoman added that some department stores with grocery areas were authorised stockists, but the clothing area was clearly segmented.

Supermarkets in Britain have targeted a range of products in the past to bring down prices, with value-for-money ASDA managing to help break fixed prices on books and currently challenging price constraints on over-the-counter medicines.
ASDA said it had no plans, however, to stock cut price Levi jeans.
"We are too busy selling our own George range of jeans," a spokesman said.
ASDA sells its George men's jeans at 16.99 pounds and 19.99 pounds per pair.
